text:
ana: Heads up — p99 latency for short-seq text-gen jumped after the batching heuristic deploy (hash c3f9a2e). Saw it start ~10:15 UTC, correlated with canary traffic. Anyone else?

mike: saw it on the dashboard too. p50 unchanged, p95 up a bit, p99 went from ~60ms -> ~340ms on hosted. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/serving/text-gen?from=now-30m :eyes:

oliver: I rolled a profiler for one of the canaries — initial flame shows a lot of time in kernel selection path and memcpy during cache loads. Attaching a snippet (from perf-bot):
```
# top stacks
runtime::serve_request
  -> batching::form_batch
  -> kvcache::load_prefix (heavy)
  -> kernel_selector::choose_path (fallback to generic)
```

jana: interesting — we changed the batch-merging threshold in the heuristic to favor larger batches earlier. That could increase KV cache evictions if many different contexts are merged. @ana do we have metrics on kv cache hit rate?

perf-bot: kv_cache_hit_rate{route="text-gen"} dropped from 0.88 to 0.61 during the canary window (10:12-10:20).

cody: also seeing token-budget queues backlog. The continuous batcher is accepting more inflight tokens per batch and pushing kernel selection to pick quantized paths less often. That would explain the increased kernel-selection overhead and slower kernels.

ana: @cody typo — you mean @cody? :) but +1. Do we have per-kernel selection counts?

oliver: yes — kernel_selector_counts last 30m: fast_attn_kernel: 48%, generic_attn: 52% (pre-deploy it was ~82% fast_attn, 18% generic). So we flipped to generic for a lot of requests.

mike: probable root cause: merging heterogenous sequence lengths caused the runtime to pick conservative kernels and to flush KV caches more often (eviction thrash). That kills short-latency tail.

ana: quick mitigation — can we gate the new merge threshold behind kv-aware policy? If not, we should rollback the heuristic to the previous value for canaries.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment c3f9a2e - rollout paused. Reason: p99 latency regression > 200ms.

oliver: I pushed a quick instrument PR with extra logs (PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4127) to dump batch compositions for failing requests. Example log: "batch_id=7a, sizes=[8,4,2], seq_lens=[16,512,12], kernels_chosen=[generic,generic,generic]"

jana: thanks. I'm running a replay of canary traffic with the kv-aware patch off to reproduce locally. If we can replicate we can test a targeted fix: prefer grouping by seq-length buckets before merging across contexts.

cody: also looking at the queue policy — token_budget_target increased from 512 -> 2048 in the change. That increases per-batch tokens and may push memory pressure. Suggest restoring to 512 for canary.

ana: agreed. Plan: 1) rollback token_budget_target to 512 on canary; 2) temporary revert of merge-threshold to previous; 3) collect batch composition + kv hit metrics; 4) iterate on kv-aware batcher that respects seq-length buckets and cache affinity. Any objections?

mike: +1. I'll open the rollback (PR/ops) and notify infra.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated (target c3f9a2e -> previous). ETA ~2m.

perf-bot: After rollback: p99 back to ~75ms, kv_cache_hit_rate back to 0.86. Throughput stable.

ana: great. Created follow-up ticket: https://tickets.redwood/ISSUE-2891 with action items (profiling, kv-aware batching, kernel tagging tests). Assigning to @oliver and @cody.

oliver: for the follow-up I want to add a kernel-compatibility tag per batch so we don't re-evaluate kernels for each individual within a merged batch (cheap heuristic). Also will add a fallback cost-estimate to avoid generic kernel blowups.

cody: I'll prototype seq-length bucketing and an eviction-aware merge policy. If that looks good we'll canary it behind a feature flag.

ana: OK closing the loop here. Thanks everyone — good catch on the mem/cpu profile signals. We'll keep the rollback and monitor for 1 hour then re-run controlled canary once we have the kv-aware patch. :thumbsup:

mike: leaving a short postmortem note in #postmortems after we finish the changes.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed successfully.
